content: 1. When preparing draft specifications, do not omit clauses, insert additional clauses, or include limits that are less stringent than those provided in the guidelines without referring to Section 4. 2. If two or more active ingredients are co-formulated, they should generally have separate specifications. However, in cases where the interactions of active ingredients or synergists in long-lasting insecticidal nets (LNs) are required and justified, a single specification encompassing multiple active ingredients or synergists should be proposed. 3. For combination LNs, specifications must be divided into one specification for each netting material and one for the finished net. 4. From the Notes provided at the end of the guideline, incorporate only those applicable to the specific specification being prepared. 5. The product must appear clean and free from visible extraneous matter, visible damage (e.g., splitting or tearing), and visible manufacturing defects (e.g., poorly made seams or non-uniform or excessively loose weaves). It must also be suitable for use as or in a long-lasting insecticidal net. 6. Each active ingredient (and synergist, if required) must comply with an identity test. If the identity remains uncertain, it must pass at least one additional test. 7. The content of active ingredients, when determined, must not deviate from the declared value by more than ±10%. 8. The dimensional stability of netting to washing must not exceed 10% shrinkage or 5% expansion in either direction. 9. The average bursting strength of the netting must not be less than the declared value. If seams are present, their average bursting strength must not be less than the average for the fabric. 10. Flammability testing must ensure that no ignition or flame propagation occurs after the removal of the igniting flame. There should be no flaming debris or ignition of filter paper. 11. Specifications may apply to manufactured nets only, bulk netting only, or both, as required. The title and description clause should be modified accordingly. 12. The linear density (denier) of the fibers cannot be measured in the manufactured net but should be identified on the packaging. 13. Long-lasting insecticidal netting is expected to retain its insecticidal activity throughout its lifespan and after multiple washes (for public health products) or under worst-case climatic conditions (for agricultural products). 14. Analytical methods must be CIPAC, AOAC, or equivalent. If unpublished, full details and appropriate validation data must be submitted to FAO/WHO. 15. Samples should be taken according to specified guidelines and must be representative of the net or netting. Testing material within 10 cm of seams or selvedges should be avoided unless seam testing is required. 16. For coated LNs, if the netting is manufactured under different deniers, the active ingredient content must be specified for each type of denier. If specified as mg/m², this should be calculated from values for active ingredient in g/kg and mass of net/m². 17. The method of analysis must be peer-validated. If unpublished, full details and peer-validation data must be provided. 18. Mesh size is determined by counting the number of holes in a defined square of fabric. Conditioning of the fabric should follow ISO 139 standards. 19. Washing and drying procedures for testing dimensional changes must follow ISO standards, including the use of specific washing machines and programs. 20. Flammability testing should follow EN 1102 standards, with observations including after-flame time, afterglow time, maximum burnt or damaged width and length, and whether flaming debris or ignition of filter paper occurs. 21. Sampling and testing must ensure that the material complies with specified requirements. Samples must be stored to prevent deterioration and protected against contamination. 22. Matrix release formulations are primarily for public health protection but may also be used in agricultural applications. They involve active ingredients incorporated into or coated onto polymers, or a combination of both methods. 23. For combination matrix release formulations, specifications should be divided into one for each polymer preparation type and one for the finished product. 24. Matrix release formulations must achieve long-lasting pest efficacy through controlled release of active ingredients in the habitat of harmful pests, such as water sources or ponds. 25. Parameters such as active ingredient selection, content, product design, and retention/release rate are critical for defining the quality of matrix release formulations and can be optimized through manufacturing processes or customer needs.
